messages:
maya: heads-up, onboarding safira-11b (float -> int4) for the bench stack. quick smoke shows a weird token insertion after merging vocabs plus rotary phase drift.
kevin: can you paste the minimal repro + tokenizer snippets? also which convert flags did you use? :eyes:
maya: ran converter: `python convert.py --src safira-11b --out safira-11b-int4 --quant int4 --merge-vocab hf-vocab.json`. small repro below.
maya: input: "Translate: Hello world"
token_ids_before_merge: [1543, 2, 345]
token_ids_after_merge:  [180, 1543, 2, 345]
logits_delta_first_token: -3.8
olivia: that extra 180 looks like an inserted sentinel/BOS. we saw similar when the tokenizer export hits surrogate pair boundaries and inserts a placeholder.
kevin: if the ids changed before quant, it's a vocab/merge issue not quant noise. try CPU fp16 reference to confirm.
maya: running CPU fp16 now, will post results. cpu run shows same insertion: `ids_before: [101, 23, 999, 2] -> ids_after_merge: [101, 180, 23, 999, 2]`. so insertion happens at merge time.
anna: found likely cause: our merge path auto-inserts unknown codepoints into the middle of the index map when iterating new_vocab bytes->str. surrogate pairs can produce a 180 placeholder in some tokenizers.
kevin: also note rotary differences: safira exports per-head rotary_scale ~1.07 for some heads; our loader assumed global shared scale=1.0. mixing assumptions shifts attention phase and amplifies small vocab errors.
maya: bench numbers (512 ctx, toy prompt): float baseline ppl=22.1, int4 convert ppl=29.4. after applying a manual id-remap patch ppl -> 23.0. suggests vocab mapping is majority of regression.
olivia: short-term: add a --safe-merge mode that preserves base indices and reports collisions instead of inserting. anna, can you post a patch?
anna: yes, small script ready: it checks tok string collisions and writes collisions to diagnostics file instead of shifting indices. will PR. snippet: `for tok, idx in new_vocab.items():
    if tok in base_vocab and base_vocab[tok] != idx:
        report_collision(tok, base_vocab[tok], idx)
    else:
        base_vocab.setdefault(tok, idx)`
maya: will re-run convert with --safe-merge and re-export rotary params with explicit per-head flag. if safe-merge fixes ids we'll focus on rotary scale handling and quant kernel noise.
kevin: long term: runtime should accept per-head rotary_scale in model metadata. opened runtime issue redwood/runtime#1289. also add a converter shim to rewrite per-head -> shared-scale for legacy runtimes.
maya: filed ticket RI-8342 with repro, logs, and gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/safira-int4-smoke. assigning to kevin/olivia/anna.
triage-bot: automated smoke run queued: safira-11b int4 -> result pre-safe-merge: fail (vocab-collisions=3, rotary-scale-drift=0.07, perf-regression=+33%). CI run link: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/RI-8342-smoke
kevin: can we add a tiny adapter that remaps kv-cache indices on the fly for exports that used the old insertion behavior? would be useful to keep rolling until exporters fixed.
maya: good call. i'll prototype a KV shim that rewrites index pointers using a collision-map. posting minimal gist after cpu run.
olivia: also add unit tests for surrogate pair handling and sentinel collisions in tokenizer export pipeline.
maya: thanks everyone, running full CI with --safe-merge now. will update when green. :thumbsup:
